S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S075.name: Social_Detachment
S075.description: Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.

subtypes.Emotional Detachment: Feeling cut off from others even when physically present, unable to feel connection.
subtypes.Social Isolation: Increasingly isolating oneself and not participating in social activities or gatherings.
subtypes.Difficulty with Intimacy: Distancing oneself from close people as it is difficult to become emotionally close.
subtypes.Loss of Belonging: Feeling like an outsider who belongs nowhere.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).

subtypes.Anhedonia for Happiness: Unable to feel happiness or joy even when good things happen.
subtypes.Lack of Satisfaction: Unable to experience satisfaction or pride even after achieving something good.
subtypes.Inability to Feel Love: Feeling numb to love or affection towards family or lovers.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where the mind feels empty and nothing is felt, as if all positive emotions are blocked.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

info.persona: Regino Estrada blends a love for orderly spreadsheets, hearty barbecue aromas, and classic‑car grease, all while quietly steering his plant toward a digital future and ensuring their family’s traditions stay sizzling; they are known for double‑checking every checklist twice.
info.professional_persona: Regino Estrada, a plant manager in industrial equipment manufacturing, leverages lean principles, statistical process control, and data‑driven decision‑making to keep production humming; they now eye a regional director role to steer multiple Texas facilities through an IoT‑enabled digital transformation while mentoring rising managers and pursuing an MBA.
info.cultural_background: Regino is a first‑generation Mexican‑American who grew up in a bilingual household, speaking Spanish at home and English at school. He maintains strong ties to Mexican traditions, celebrating Día de los Muertos, preparing tamales for holidays, and infusing Mexican flavors into his cooking. Living in Liberty Hill, Texas, he integrates these cultural practices with local ranching and outdoor lifestyles, participating in both Mexican community events and broader county festivities. His Catholic faith and deep emphasis on family cohesion reflect the values instilled by his parents and the broader Mexican heritage.
info.hobbies_and_interests: During his free time, Regino enjoys hosting family barbecues that blend Mexican home‑cooking with Texas brisket, emphasizing communal meals and tradition. He is an avid fisherman, frequently casting lines at lakes and rivers around Burnet County. Community service is important to him, and he volunteers at his local church and helps organize the town’s annual Cinco de Mayo celebration. He also restores classic cars as a hands‑on hobby, watches high school football games with friends, and reads historical non‑fiction to unwind.
info.sports_persona: Regino Estrada is a dedicated fan of the Burnet High School Bulldogs football team, regularly attends Friday night games with a small crew of friends, follows the Dallas Cowboys and Texas Rangers for professional thrills, and spends weekend mornings casting lines at Lake Buchanan as part of the Burnet County anglers' club; they often discuss game stats and fishing knots over a cold beer.
info.arts_persona: Regino Estrada unwinds by devouring historical nonfiction from authors like David McCullough and Doris Kearns Goodwin, enjoys classic rock icons such as Bruce Springsteen and southern country legend Willie Nelson, and frequently attends regional classic‑car shows where they admire the craftsmanship of 1950s Chevrolet designs.
info.travel_persona: Regino Estrada prefers well‑planned road trips that blend relaxation and discovery, often escaping to the Hill Country vineyards of Fredericksburg or the art‑laden streets of Santa Fe, while keeping a careful eye on travel costs to ensure their family’s annual budget still supports their upcoming MBA program; they usually map out each itinerary on a spreadsheet before hitting the road.
info.culinary_persona: Regino Estrada boasts an intermediate‑to‑advanced kitchen skill set, expertly marrying smoky Texas brisket rubs with piquant home‑cooked spices like chipotle, cumin, and fresh cilantro to create crowd‑pleasing barbecues that feature dishes such as smoked brisket, carne asada tacos, and hearty chili con carne; they never miss a chance to pair them with locally sourced jalapeños and avocado slices.

info.persona: Chanelle Russell is a competitive, curiosity‑driven operations veteran whose love of art and salsa offsets a chronic worry‑about‑details habit, making them both meticulous and delightfully eclectic.
info.professional_persona: Chanelle Russell leverages three decades of operations leadership across retail, manufacturing, and service sectors, using Lean Six Sigma and data‑driven analysis to drive continuous improvement while championing mentorship for women and people of color and integrating local arts into workplace culture.
info.cultural_background: Chanelle grew up in Indianapolis as part of a close-knit African-American community that celebrated music, storytelling, and civic engagement. Her family’s roots trace back to the Great Migration, and she was raised on the traditions of Juneteenth celebrations, church choir singing, and neighborhood block parties on Indiana Avenue, a historic hub for jazz and Black entrepreneurship. These experiences instilled a deep appreciation for cultural expression and a commitment to uplift the next generation of Black professionals. While she never married, her network of extended family, church, and community organizations has provided a strong support system that shapes her identity and informs her leadership style.
info.hobbies_and_interests: A lifelong lover of the arts, Chanelle frequently visits the Indianapolis Museum of Art and attends community-theater productions and jazz concerts. She participates in a weekly salsa-dance class, enjoys cooking experimental dishes in a local culinary club, and tends to a small urban garden that provides a calming outlet from work stress. Her curiosity leads her to join a book-club focused on nonfiction and social-justice topics, travel to cities known for their cultural heritage, and volunteer as a mentor for young professionals through a local Black women’s business network.
info.sports_persona: Chanelle Russell supports the Indiana Pacers and Indianapolis Colts, follows the Indianapolis 500 each May, and stays active by participating in a senior tennis league at the Indianapolis Racquet Club while also maintaining her weekly salsa‑dance class, which she treats as both social workout and cultural immersion.
info.arts_persona: Chanelle Russell immerses herself in the arts by frequenting the Indianapolis Museum of Art for exhibitions by artists like Kara Walker, attending community‑theater productions at The Repertory Theatre of Indianapolis, reveling in live jazz shows headlined by Wynton Marsalis, and channeling that inspiration into her weekly salsa‑dance sessions.
info.travel_persona: Chanelle Russell curates her travel around cultural hubs, having explored New Orleans’ jazz scene, Kyoto’s historic temples, and Barcelona’s modernist architecture, while planning a future trip to Florence to study Renaissance art, balancing her itinerary with a modest travel budget and occasional family obligations.
info.culinary_persona: Chanelle Russell showcases her culinary curiosity in the Indy Food Explorers club by mastering miso‑glazed black cod, charred cauliflower tacos, and saffron risotto, favoring ingredients like smoked paprika, sumac, and garden‑fresh basil and thyme, and often experiments with molecular gastronomy techniques at home.

info.persona: Jesse Dent, a disciplined yet curious retiree who meticulously catalogues every garden seed, vintage radio part, and family genealogy detail, but occasionally misplaces their glasses while searching for a misplaced screwdriver, they embody a life of orderly curiosity tempered by charming absent‑mindedness.
info.professional_persona: Jesse Dent, a retired handyman‑turned‑community volunteer, applies decades of home‑repair, woodworking, and event‑planning expertise with disciplined organization and a practical curiosity, and they have become the go‑to advisor for neighbors seeking reliable solutions.
info.cultural_background: Jesse grew up in the post‑war suburban environment of New Jersey, part of a white, middle‑class American culture that values self‑reliance, community involvement, and modest prosperity. His upbringing in Ramsey, Bergen County, was shaped by the Northeastern United States’s emphasis on punctuality, order, and a strong work ethic. Family traditions include celebrating major holidays with home‑cooked meals, attending local church events, and an appreciation for American history, particularly the Revolutionary and Civil War eras. These cultural influences, combined with the diverse community offerings of the area, have nurtured his balanced curiosity and practical outlook.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Jesse enjoys a variety of hobbies that reflect his curiosity and practical nature, such as gardening (especially growing tomatoes and roses), building and operating model train layouts, reading historical nonfiction, researching genealogy, volunteering at the local library and senior center, walking his dog in nearby parks, playing bridge and card games with friends, watching classic films, and restoring vintage radios.
info.sports_persona: Jesse Dent, a regular attendee of New York Mets spring training broadcasts and a devoted New York Giants fan during football season, they stay fit through daily dog walks in the Ramsey Parks, seasonal gardening, and participation in the local senior walking club.
info.arts_persona: Jesse Dent, an aficionado of classic cinema such as Casablanca and John Ford’s The Searchers, they enjoy listening to Frank Sinatra and Ella Fitzgerald while restoring vintage radios, and occasionally attend productions at the nearby Alpine Theatre featuring works by playwrights like Arthur Miller.
info.travel_persona: Jesse Dent, who has meticulously planned road trips to the Revolutionary War sites of Boston, Philadelphia, and Gettysburg, and dreams of a transatlantic pilgrimage to the historic streets of Bath and the D‑Day beaches of Normandy, they favor detailed itineraries that balance guided tours with relaxed scenic drives.
info.culinary_persona: Jesse Dent, an intermediate home cook who loves canning heirloom tomatoes into rustic marinara, whipping up rosemary‑roasted chicken and apple pie for family gatherings, and savoring a hearty corn chowder seasoned with fresh basil and garden‑grown garlic, they often balance these meals with occasional visits to the neighborhood diner for a classic cheeseburger.
